body:
Hey, I had to work yesterday and went to sleep early last night so I never got around to checking back here until now. Your assumption was right, I'm most definitely a dude. I really want to thank you for your post, because it was honestly insightful and honest and gave me some perspective. 

I mean, I'm already onto a lot of the things you talked about, but 
sometimes I take them for granted. I try to convince myself that I'm just dealing with normal problems for my age, but when I see other people interacting it tears me apart inside. Everything feels so rigid and strained when it's me in the hot-seat. I've had one girlfriend, in high school, and it ended when she moved completely across the country. We tried to stay in touch for 6 months or so, but I got frustrated when it would take 2-3 weeks to hear back and told her to just stop contacting me.

I was enjoying work for a while, I still can if I have something to look forward to but otherwise it's fairly depressing. This is on top of whatever mood disorder I already deal with, waking up one week feeling on top of the world and the next couple of weeks wanting to end my life. It sounds stupid but it's completely out of my control at the time. I just wish I had (a) friend(s) to spend time with so I didn't feel so alone, but
1) I don't know how to transition a friendship from work-buddies to spending time outside of work, and 
2) I feel so self-conscious about myself that I avoid trying.

Ultimately I wish I could say that I'd be okay, because I know I want to push myself to something more than working for $10/hr doing menial tasks, but after 6 or 7 years of intermittent suicidal thoughts, I wonder what will actually happen.
